name: Sequence Diagram
description: Sequence Diagram describes the time-ordered interaction between actors, objects, UI, components, services, or databases. This diagram answers the question: who calls whom, in what order, and with what response.
purpose: Detailed technical design for API flows, transactions, or inter-service interactions.
bestFor: Detailed technical design of API or transaction flows
Describe OAuth2, payment, and ordering flows
Provide backend documentation for service, repository, and database call order
notSuitableFor: Describe cross-departmental business workflow → use Activity Diagram
Describe object lifecycle states → use State Machine Diagram
Describe static class/entity relationships → use Class Diagram
useCases: Identify the actor/system that starts the flow
Number messages sequentially along the vertical axis
Identify message type: sync, async, return
Add combined fragments: alt, opt, loop, par
Add return messages with response data
requirements: Combined fragments — alt, opt, loop, par (optional)

elements.name: Message
elements.description: Call between lifelines: POST /login, SQL query

elements.name: Return Message
elements.description: Response from a call: JWT token, error message

elements.name: Activation Bar
elements.description: Time during which a lifeline is processing a message

confusableWith.difference: Sequence focuses on messages between lifelines; Activity focuses on workflow/action.
Sequence emphasizes time order; Communication emphasizes object links.
